recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Address FHIR-50625 and FHIR-50626 only after separate work-group disposition; do not reopen FHIR-38921 to make new semantic edits.
issue_request: FHIR-38921 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification R5 FHIR-core issue asking Subscriptions to clarify reliable versus unreliable delivery, including consequences for notifications and topics. The final resolution was to add an extension indicating that a channel should be treated as non-guaranteed, effectively labeling the subscription as best effort.
initial_application: Core commit 9a1651d176f8e6d1adda6336f463d4ffe3f8d224 added the best-effort versus guaranteed delivery section and related wording to source/subscriptions.html. Extension-pack commit e503dcaf2dd470993cfe072bfa4112e0d891c5ed added StructureDefinition/subscription-best-effort with the final non-guaranteed delivery definition referenced by the Jira resolution.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Subscription, SubscriptionStatus, and SubscriptionTopic as active resources, and source/hierarchy.xml includes subscriptions.html in the current page hierarchy. Current SubscriptionStatus notes carry the related event-numbering guidance. Later R6 Jira issues FHIR-50625 and FHIR-50626 raise unresolved consistency questions, but they are Triaged and do not provide a final decision that would supersede FHIR-38921.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No core source edit was made because the core clarification is already present and the final extension artifact belongs to, and exists in, the FHIR Extension Pack rather than this core checkout.
